output.title: When bookkeeping habits become busywork
output.body:
For a small-business owner, the real question is not whether bookkeeping should exist. It is whether a weekly bookkeeping habit is still helping the business, or just creating tidy-looking busywork.

That is a bounded workflow decision. If the same task shows up every week, depends on memory, and produces the same output each time, it is worth checking whether manual effort is still the right tool. If it is not repetitive or it changes too much from week to week, leave it alone. No need to automate a moving target.

A simple next step is to pick one bookkeeping task and write down three things: the input, the decision rule, and the output. For example, an invoice lands in email, a person decides the category, and the line is entered into the sheet. If you can write that chain clearly, you have a real candidate for a bounded workflow change. If you cannot, the habit may be doing more thinking than the business needs.

That is the limit to watch: not “bookkeeping” in general, but one repeated task that consumes attention without adding judgment. Some chores deserve a machine; some deserve a calendar reminder and a mug of tea.
